effect_mechanism: Terraces, contour stone bunds and spate or diversion structures slow and spread runoff, lowering peak discharges and lengthening flood rise times; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment clipped peak discharges, doubled base time and cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50%, and small reservoirs are perceived by users to limit rainy-season floods [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1].
conditionality: Direction depends on design: diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes increased peak flows, dike failure risks gullying, and larger sand dams increase flooding risk [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. Catchment-scale evidence is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain, the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported assertions without measurement [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].

effect_mechanism: Water harvesting and conservation structures capture runoff and raise soil moisture in the root zone, so rainfed crops yield more, especially in dry years and low-rainfall areas; stored water also enables supplemental irrigation, extra crop cycles and diversification, zaï and stone lines trap sediment, manure and organic matter, and terracing levels slopes to retain moisture. In Burkina Faso stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55%, and by about 142% with compost, while in drought years zaï and tassa fields produced a harvest where untreated land gave little or none [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s].
conditionality: The pool mixes independent evaluations (IFPRI/ESSP matching studies in Ethiopia, a DIME difference-in-difference in Rwanda) with lender self-reported completion-report figures and bundled watershed programmes in which SWC works came with seed, fertiliser and crop packages, so the share attributable to the structures is unclear. Null or negative results are present: SWC promoted mostly off-farm had no yield effect, late adopters and the pooled sample in Ethiopia showed no significant gain, bunds lowered yields in high-rainfall Amhara, zaï lowered sorghum yields under waterlogging in humid Cameroon, and diversion banquettes in Niger cut yields. Zaï pits alone gave an average sorghum gain of only 38 kg/ha in one study against 310 kg/ha in another, so much of the benefit rides on the manure or compost added, and benefits can take several years of maintained structures to appear [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_2, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_3].
